claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex - he's 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 19 years old, there are some specific conditions that apply. Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 in certain circumstances.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar courses) or on an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know, thank you.

Since Alex is 19 and studying A-levels, I have a couple more questions to determine eligibility:

**When did Alex turn 19, and when did he start (or re-enrol in) this A-level course?** 

This is important because there are rules about when the course must have started in relation to the child's age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 19 back in February, and he started the A-level course in September last year when he was still 18. He's been continuing with it since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for those details. That's helpful.

I have one more important question:

**Does Alex live with you, or if not, do you contribute financially towards his upkeep (such as paying for food, accommodation, or other living costs)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

I just have a couple more questions to complete the eligibility check:

**Are you (the person who would be claiming the benefit) responsible for Alex? In other words, are you his parent or do you have parental responsibility for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent - I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me also check the specific guidance about Child Benefit when a child turns 16 to confirm the rules around education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 19 years old (turned 19 in February)
- He is studying A-levels at a sixth form college (which is full-time non-advanced education)
- He started the course in September last year when he was still 18
- He lives with you
- You are his parent and responsible for him

Let me now provide you with the eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **Age**: Alex is 19, which is under 20 years old  
✅ **Education**: A-levels count as full-time non-advanced education, which qualifies for Child Benefit  
✅ **Course start date**: Alex started his A-level course before he turned 19 (he enrolled in September when he was 18)  
✅ **Responsibility**: You are his parent and he lives with you  

**Important things to note:**
- You'll need to inform HMRC that Alex is continuing in education so your Child Benefit payments continue
- Your eligibility will continue until Alex completes his course or turns 20, whichever comes first
- If Alex starts receiving Universal Credit or begins paid work of 24 hours or more per week, eligibility would stop

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

reasonings: Alex is 19 years old, which is under the age of 20. He is in full-time non-advanced education (A-levels at a sixth form college), which qualifies for Child Benefit. Crucially, he was accepted onto the A-level course in September last year when he was still 18, which meets the requirement that the child must be accepted onto the course before they turn 19. He lives with his parent who is responsible for him, satisfying the responsibility requirement. As long as Alex does not receive Universal Credit or other disqualifying benefits, and continues in this approved education, Child Benefit eligibility continues until he completes the course or turns 20 (whichever comes first).
